evidence.note: Strong opening arc: climb (T3) into 'Hitman snaps off missile dropkick — Hall takes 19 damage' with real position play (TOP_ROPE vs RUNNING_ROPES on T3-T4).
Hall reaches 1 HP on T55 and the match then runs 155 more turns without resolution; HP alone cannot finish, so the middle of the match has no stakes gradient at all.

Loop tax fires but does not break the loop: 'The repeated tie-up stalls out — Hall gains escape momentum' with player momentum draining 5→2 across T89/T91/T93, and the player simply re-enters the tie-up each time (49 collar-and-elbow uses total, move_repetition_rate 0.4667).
Same two-move exchange still running at T187-T200: tie-up → 'Hall uses the stale tie-up to reset with momentum' → tie-up, with health frozen at [55, 6] for a dozen turns.

Only real climax is the last 8 turns: three straight Razor's Edge hits (T204/T206/T208) with '— FINISHER — the next cover packs extra heat', dropping Hitman 46→1; a genuine comeback beat, but arriving after ~150 turns of stalemate and with near_fall_count=0.
Curated menu is honest about the new tax up front: collar-and-elbow note reads 'enter a tie-up to unlock throws and whips; repeat loops lose steam' before any loop has formed.

Warning escalates legibly in the menu itself — note flips to 'tie-up is going stale — pay it off or reset before they steal momentum' on 24 turns (T31 through T201), matched in the log by 'The repeated tie-up stalls out — Hall gains escape momentum'.
Opponent side of the tax is equally readable: 'Hall uses the stale tie-up to reset with momentum' explains why the grapple evaporated instead of silently ending.

Groggy is presented as a modifier, not a position: 'Hitman is GROGGY — power moves and finishers are live!' with state position STANDING and groggy=[true,false]; T205 follow-up 'Hitman rises — still groggy from the impact!' keeps pending-groggy legible.
Readability nit: on a player turn the only log line is 'Hall turns the tables!', so the actor of the printed outcome is ambiguous; same phrasing appears for the player on T94.

Pin is visible whenever legal (offered T7/19/39/75/79/109/119/141/145/165, curation_pin_visible=true), but its note stays static — 'try to end it now; stronger when they're worn down' — with no cue that Hall has been at 1 HP since T55.

The interesting unexplored branch is explicit in the menu: 'Cover — pinfall attempt' and 'Sharpshooter (89%)' both offered while Hall sits at 1 HP, and the methodical policy took index 3 'Climb to the top rope' instead.
The same Finish/Set-up fork reappears at T109/T119/T141/T145/T165 and is declined every time; the match's only real question is what happens if the offered finish is actually cashed in.

Session ends on a 210-turn slog with log_uniqueness_ratio 0.2096 and the top log line repeated 22 times ('Hitman: Collar-and-elbow tie-up.'), which suppresses appetite for an immediate rerun of this policy.

stickiness.rematch_reason: The finish run (T202-T210) and the momentum-drain feedback are genuinely interesting, but 150 turns of tie-up/break stalemate against a 1 HP opponent is exhausting and I would not replay this policy as-is.
stickiness.next_experiment: Rerun seed 216 with a policy that takes the Finish intent the first time it appears while the opponent is worn down (pin/sharpshooter were offered at T75 and T79) to see whether the match resolves in-band instead of stalling out.

evidence.note: Big-spot text lands early: 'Hitman snaps off missile dropkick — Hall takes 19 damage' with position shifting to GROUNDED.
Payoff feel collapses mid-match: 'Hitman snaps off side headlock — Hall takes 6 damage' takes Hall to 1 HP and nothing in the text or state marks it as a near-finish moment.

Narrative freshness is very low — log_uniqueness_ratio 0.2096, with 'The repeated tie-up stalls out — Hall gains escape momentum' printed 21 times and 'Hall uses the stale tie-up to reset with momentum' 16 times; the anti-loop copy itself becomes the most repetitive line in the match.

Finisher beat is strong when it finally lands: 'Hall snaps off razor's edge — Hitman takes 20 damage. / Hitman is rattled — when they're forced up, big payoffs may open. / — FINISHER — the next cover packs extra heat.'

Pin sequence is well paced (finish_sequence delays 0.0/1.0/1.5) and callbacks the finisher — 'The finisher still echoes — +12 on the cover!' — but it is a clean 1…2…3 with near_fall_count=0, so there is no kickout drama anywhere in 210 turns.

top_issues.summary: The loop tax is legible but does not actually break the loop: the player used collar-and-elbow 49 times, ate 21 'repeated tie-up stalls out' penalties (T31 through T199), and still re-entered the tie-up at 60-94% every time because it stays the top curated Grapple control option with no cooldown or gating.
top_issues.suggested_area: Grapple re-entry gating / escalating cost or lockout after repeated stale tie-ups

top_issues.summary: Hall sits at 1 HP from T55 to T210 (155 turns) while HP recovery ticks him back to 6 and 11; nothing in log or state escalates urgency for a nearly-beaten opponent, so the match has a dead midgame with no stakes signal.
top_issues.suggested_area: Low-HP urgency state / forced finish pressure when a wrestler is near zero

top_issues.summary: Pacing gate failed at 210 turns (band [8, 40]) with near_fall_count=0 and log_uniqueness_ratio 0.2096; the entire match arc is compressed into the last 8 turns (T202-T210).
top_issues.suggested_area: Match-length pressure / escalating damage or fatigue over turn count

top_issues.summary: On T193 a player turn prints only 'Hall turns the tables!' (and T94 prints 'Hitman turns the tables!' on a CPU turn), so reversal lines do not make clear who acted and who benefited.
